feature_preprocessing.note: sqa_features.combined_vector (per-modality SQI pack ++ advanced dynamics/HOS); pure numpy (numpy.rfft only); graph z-scores x_raw and standardizes x_feat (baked).

calibration.evaluation_partition: validation (store_ppg4_tmb) — the same split the temperature grid was minimized on; see held_out_ece for the held-out measurement
calibration.partition_note: the ECE pairs above are measured on the SAME validation split the temperature grid was minimized on, so the post-scaling number is an optimization minimum and optimistic. held_out_ece below is the held-out measurement: on 874 store_v8 test windows from 146 subjects this graph never saw, the grade head's post-scaling ECE is 0.1253 -- 2.41x the 0.052 above, the largest optimism gap of the four shipped cards. The usable head holds up (0.0465 vs 0.0283).

held_out_ece.partition: data/store_v8 test split, restricted to subjects absent from both the train and val partitions of data/store_ppg4_tmb (this graph's training store)
held_out_ece.population_kind: within_distribution: held-out SUBJECTS of all 4 cohorts the model trained on

full_store_v8_test_partition.why_not_the_headline: 61.0% of these windows belong to subjects that were in store_ppg4_tmb's train or val partition -- store.py::_subject_split re-shuffles each cohort's subject list per build, so a store_v8 test subject is not automatically unseen by this graph

held_out_ece.pair_convention: [pre_scaling, as_shipped], same as grade_ece/usable_ece above. The graph emits raw_logits/T, so the pre-scaling logits are recovered exactly as graph_logits * T -- no model was loaded and the baked-in temperature is unchanged.
held_out_ece.estimator: biosqa.xdomain.calibration.expected_calibration_error at its default n_bins=15 (equal-width top-1-confidence bins) -- the same function and bin count that produced grade_ece/usable_ece above, so the two columns are comparable
held_out_ece.measured_by: scripts/measure_heldout_calibration.py (onnxruntime forward over this .onnx; trains nothing, exports nothing)

routing: grade+usable <- raw trunk fused with host combined SQI+dynamics vector; grade = ordinal ordered-logit

data.cohorts_note: store dataset_keys, verified against data/store_ppg4_tmb/segments.parquet (dataset_key values for modality=ppg). Same four cohorts as 'training_data_provenance.cohorts', which spells them with their display names.
data.note: added PPG-DaLiA (4th cohort) -> held-out WESAD cross-cohort LODO QWK ~0.40->~0.60; transferable-fold (WESAD/DaLiA) usable-AUROC ~0.80-0.85 (competitive with published pairwise DaLiA->WESAD band); grade ECE 0.052. Tumbling windows (50% overlap tested and found accuracy-neutral -> not used). DaLiA/WESAD share an ACC-motion label rule (caveat).

input_contract.reports: quality of the signal AS PROVIDED — if the input was pre-filtered, this is the post-filter quality
input_contract.caveat: a pre-filtered but still-corrupted signal can be under-flagged (false-clean): an aggressive low-pass/band-limit strips the high-frequency cues the model keys on. The app runs biosqa.inference.prefilter.detect_prefiltering() to warn when the input looks pre-filtered.

novelty.reference_note: the reference manifold was fit on store_v6, which predates PPG-DaLiA, while this model trained on store_ppg4_tmb (which includes it) — the reference is therefore not this model's training corpus. Measured effect: 0/250 sampled DaLiA windows exceed d2_threshold (median D2 3.11 vs the 63.78 cutoff), lower than the in-reference BUT PPG cohort's 4.0% flag rate. Regenerated by scripts/fit_novelty_constants.py, which reproduces the shipped d2_threshold from store_v6 exactly (ecg 36.9192, eda 28.3858, ppg 63.7819).
